description: Checks core accounting knowledge: double entry, financial statements, reconciliations, adjustments and ethical practice.

competencies.name: Double-entry and journals
competencies.description: Applies debits and credits correctly to common transactions

competencies.name: Financial statements
competencies.description: Understands the financial statements and the accrual basis

competencies.name: Reconciliations and internal controls
competencies.description: Reconciles records and detects errors and irregularities

competencies.name: Accruals, prepayments and adjustments
competencies.description: Handles prepayments, depreciation and allowances

competencies.name: Accounting practice and ethics
competencies.description: Follows sound practice, honesty and the imprest system

questions.text: A school receives TZS 500,000 cash from a parent for fees that were already invoiced earlier. Which entry is correct?

options.text: Debit Fees receivable, credit Cash
Debit Cash, credit Fees receivable (debtors)
Debit Cash, credit Fee income again, as the income is earned when paid
Debit Fee income, credit Fees receivable

questions.explanation: The fee income was recorded when the invoice was raised. Receiving the cash increases Cash and reduces the amount owed by the parent.

questions.text: Which financial statement shows a school's assets, liabilities and equity at one particular date?

options.text: Statement of cash flows
Income and expenditure statement (surplus or deficit)
Trial balance of the year
Statement of financial position (balance sheet)

questions.explanation: The statement of financial position lists what the school owns, what it owes and the accumulated funds at a date. The other statements cover a period or are not financial statements.

questions.text: On 1 October a school pays TZS 1,200,000 for 12 months of insurance. The financial year ends on 31 December. How much is prepaid at year-end?
questions.explanation: Three months (Oct-Dec) are used, leaving nine months unused: 9 x 100,000 = 900,000, which is shown as a prepayment (current asset).

questions.text: Which of these can explain a difference between the cash book balance and the bank statement balance at month-end? Select all that apply.

options.text: A deposit made on the last day that the bank has not yet credited
A cheque issued by the school that the bank has not yet paid
Depreciation of equipment not yet posted
A supplier invoice received but not yet paid
Bank charges that are not yet recorded in the cash book

questions.explanation: Timing differences and bank items not yet in the cash book appear in a bank reconciliation. Unpaid invoices and depreciation do not involve the bank account.

questions.text: Under the accrual basis of accounting, when is an expense recognised?

options.text: Only on the day the money actually leaves the school's bank account
When the order is placed with the supplier
When the supplier sends a payment reminder
When it is incurred, even if it has not yet been paid

questions.explanation: Accrual accounting matches expenses to the period in which the goods or services were used, regardless of when cash is paid.

questions.text: A school has debtors of TZS 10,000,000. The allowance for doubtful debts is currently TZS 300,000 and must be increased to TZS 500,000. What is charged to expenses this year?
questions.explanation: Only the increase in the allowance is charged to the income statement: 500,000 - 300,000 = 200,000.

questions.text: A trial balance agrees (debits equal credits). Which error would still NOT be revealed by it?

options.text: A debit entry posted but the matching credit left out of the ledger completely
A debit of TZS 45,000 posted as TZS 54,000 only
A purchase of stationery posted to the repairs expense account
A credit entry posted twice with one debit

questions.explanation: Posting to the wrong account of the right type keeps debits equal to credits. The other errors make the two totals different.

questions.text: While preparing a bank reconciliation you find a TZS 800,000 withdrawal on the bank statement that is not in the cash book and nobody can explain it. What should you do?

options.text: Report it to the accountant or head and ask the bank for the supporting document
Record it as a miscellaneous expense so the books balance and the reconciliation closes
Leave it in the reconciliation until the year-end audit
Ask the cashier to correct the cash book without telling anyone

questions.explanation: Unexplained bank items may be errors or fraud. They must be reported and investigated, not hidden in an expense account.

questions.text: The school buys 5 desks for TZS 750,000 and the supplier gives 30 days to pay. The invoice is not yet paid. Which entry is correct?

options.text: Debit Furniture, credit Cash
Debit Furniture, credit Creditors (accounts payable)
Debit Furniture expense, credit Fee income for the term
Debit Creditors, credit Furniture

questions.explanation: The desks are an asset, and the school now owes the supplier, so a liability (creditors) is created instead of reducing cash.

questions.text: Last month's books are closed. A manager asks you to change the date of a TZS 2,000,000 expense so that it appears in last month and next month looks better. What is the best response?

options.text: Agree, because the manager is responsible for the results of the school
Agree if it is only a small amount for the school
Change the date and add a note in your own file
Decline, record it with its true date and tell your supervisor

questions.explanation: Records must show when transactions really happened. Changing dates to influence results is misreporting, so it should be declined and escalated.

questions.text: A board member notes that the income statement shows a surplus of TZS 3,000,000, but the bank balance is very low. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Some fees are invoiced but not yet collected, and cash was used to buy equipment
The surplus must always equal the bank balance, so a mistake was made in the accounts
The bank has made an error and should be contacted
Depreciation has reduced the cash in the bank account

questions.explanation: A surplus is income earned minus expenses incurred. Unpaid fees and cash spent on assets reduce cash without reducing the surplus.

questions.text: The petty cash float is TZS 100,000 under the imprest system. Paid vouchers total TZS 62,000 and the box holds TZS 38,000. What should be done to restore the float?

options.text: Do nothing, because the cash left in the box is already the correct amount
Reimburse TZS 38,000 and keep the vouchers for later
Reimburse TZS 62,000 against the approved vouchers
Add TZS 100,000 more so the box holds TZS 138,000

questions.explanation: Under an imprest system the cash plus vouchers always equals the float, and the vouchers total is refunded to restore it.

description: Checks daily record keeping, cash book, ledger posting, trial balance and bank reconciliation skills.

competencies.name: Source documents and records
competencies.description: Identifies source documents and records transactions from valid evidence

competencies.name: Cash book and petty cash
competencies.description: Keeps the cash book and petty cash with proper vouchers

competencies.name: Ledgers and double entry
competencies.description: Posts to ledgers using debits and credits and corrects errors properly

competencies.name: Trial balance and error finding
competencies.description: Prepares a trial balance and traces differences

competencies.name: Bank reconciliation
competencies.description: Prepares bank reconciliations

questions.text: Which of these are source documents for bookkeeping entries? Select all that apply.

options.text: A trial balance
A statement of financial position
A supplier invoice
A bank deposit slip
A ledger account

questions.explanation: Source documents are the original evidence of transactions. The trial balance, ledger and statements are records prepared from them.

questions.text: What does "double entry" mean in bookkeeping?

options.text: Every transaction is written twice in the same book, once by each of two different clerks
Two people must sign every entry in the cash book
Each transaction is copied to a second book for safety
Every transaction is recorded in at least two accounts, with equal debits and credits

questions.explanation: In double entry each transaction has a debit effect and a credit effect of equal value.

questions.text: In a two-column or three-column cash book, where is money received recorded?

options.text: On the debit side
On the credit side
Only in the narrative column
In the balance column only

questions.explanation: Cash is an asset, so receipts are debited and payments are credited in the cash book.

questions.text: Which of these accounts normally have a debit balance? Select all that apply.

options.text: Fee income
Cash at bank
Furniture
Creditors (accounts payable)
Rent expense

questions.explanation: Assets and expenses normally have debit balances. Income, liabilities and capital normally have credit balances.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a trial balance?

options.text: To prove that there are no errors of any kind in the ledger accounts
To show the school's profit for the year only
To list all payments made through the bank
To check that total debit balances equal total credit balances

questions.explanation: A trial balance tests the arithmetic of double entry, but some errors can remain even when it agrees.

questions.text: The cash book shows TZS 1,000,000. The bank statement shows bank charges of TZS 15,000 that are not yet in the cash book. What is the correct updated cash book balance?
questions.explanation: Bank charges reduce the bank balance, so the cash book must be reduced: 1,000,000 - 15,000 = 985,000.

questions.text: A trial balance is out by TZS 20,000 and the debit total is too low. Which is a possible cause?

options.text: A credit of TZS 20,000 was never posted to the ledger
A debit of TZS 20,000 was posted twice
A debit of TZS 20,000 was never posted to the ledger
A purchase was posted to the wrong expense account

questions.explanation: If debits are too low, a debit was left out (or a credit was posted twice). A wrong-account error does not change the totals.

questions.text: A teacher asks for TZS 15,000 from petty cash for transport and says the receipt will come later. What should you do?

options.text: Pay only against a petty cash voucher approved by the authorised person
Pay now and record the payment in the cash book when the receipt arrives
Pay now and write "miscellaneous" in the cash book
Refuse to give petty cash to any teacher

questions.explanation: Every petty cash payment needs an approved voucher so it can be supported, recorded correctly and checked.

questions.text: A parent shows an M-Pesa message saying he paid TZS 300,000 fees, but you cannot see it on the school's mobile money statement. What should you do?

options.text: Issue the receipt, because the message is proof of payment
Do not issue a receipt or record it until the payment is verified with the provider
Record it in the cash book now and check it against the statement at the month-end close
Ask the parent to pay again and claim a refund later

questions.explanation: Messages can be forged or sent in error. Money is recorded only when it is confirmed in the school's own statement.

questions.text: You posted the school's electricity bill to the Water expense account by mistake. What is the best way to correct it?

options.text: Erase the original entry and write it again in the correct account
Delete the page and re-create it without a note
Leave it until the auditors find it
Make a correcting journal entry with a clear explanation

questions.explanation: Records must keep an audit trail, so errors are corrected by a journal (debit Electricity, credit Water) and not by erasing.

questions.text: Your trial balance does not agree, and you have already re-added the columns. What is the best next step?

options.text: Check if the difference equals one entry or half of one, then trace postings
Put the difference in a suspense account and treat the trial balance as agreed
Adjust the cash balance by the difference so that the totals agree
Start the entire year's books again from January and ignore the old ones

questions.explanation: A difference equal to one entry suggests an omission, and half of an entry suggests a debit/credit reversed. A suspense account is only a temporary place to hold a difference until it is found.

questions.text: The cash book balance is TZS 2,400,000. The bank statement shows TZS 2,560,000. Unpresented cheques are TZS 300,000. The only other difference is an uncredited deposit. How much is that deposit?
questions.explanation: Bank balance 2,560,000 - cheques 300,000 + deposit = cash book 2,400,000, so the deposit is 140,000.

description: Checks knowledge of Tanzanian payroll deductions, net pay, statutory remittance, payroll controls and staff changes.

competencies.name: Statutory deductions and contributions
competencies.description: Knows which deductions and employer contributions exist, who collects them and who pays

competencies.name: Gross-to-net pay and payslips
competencies.description: Calculates net pay and handles payslip queries

competencies.name: Statutory returns and remittance
competencies.description: Understands statutory returns, remittance and the consequences of delay

competencies.name: Payroll controls and fraud prevention
competencies.description: Applies payroll controls and responds to suspected fraud

competencies.name: Starters, leavers and changes
competencies.description: Processes new staff, leavers and changes correctly

questions.text: Which of these are costs paid by the employer and NOT deducted from the employee's salary? Select all that apply.

options.text: Workers Compensation Fund (WCF) contribution
The employee's share of the pension contribution
PAYE (income tax on employment)
Skills and Development Levy (SDL)
HESLB student loan repayment

questions.explanation: WCF and SDL are employer obligations. PAYE, the employee's pension share and HESLB loan repayments are deducted from the employee's pay.

questions.text: How is an employee's net pay calculated?

options.text: Basic salary plus all allowances paid to the employee in the month
Gross pay minus the employer's contributions
Gross pay plus the employer's contributions
Gross pay minus all deductions taken from the employee

questions.explanation: Net pay is the amount the employee receives after PAYE, the employee pension share and other authorised deductions are taken from gross pay.

questions.text: Which authority collects PAYE from employers in Tanzania?

options.text: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
National Social Security Fund (NSSF)
Workers Compensation Fund (WCF)
The local government authority

questions.explanation: PAYE is income tax, and employers withhold it and pay it to the TRA.

questions.text: Which fund is the social security scheme for public servants, such as teachers employed by the government?

options.text: Workers Compensation Fund (WCF)
Skills and Development Levy fund
Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF)
Higher Education Students' Loans Board (HESLB)

questions.explanation: PSSSF covers public servants, while NSSF mainly covers private-sector employees.

questions.text: An employer deducts PAYE from salaries but does not pay it to TRA by the deadline. What is the likely result?

options.text: Nothing happens, because each employee pays their own tax when filing at year-end
The employees become liable for the unpaid amount
TRA automatically waives the penalty for schools
The employer becomes liable for penalties and interest on the late payment

questions.explanation: Tax withheld belongs to the authority. Late payment makes the employer liable for penalties and interest.

questions.text: Which controls help prevent "ghost workers" on a payroll? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pay all salaries in cash to avoid bank records
Compare the payroll list with HR staff records every month
Let the payroll clerk change bank details without approval
Have someone other than the preparer approve the payroll
Verify staff identity and attendance from time to time

questions.explanation: Reconciling with HR, separating preparation from approval and checking that staff exist all reduce ghost-worker fraud. Uncontrolled changes and cash payments increase risk.

questions.text: Gross pay is TZS 900,000. Deductions: PAYE 50,000, employee pension 45,000, HESLB 30,000 and staff loan 25,000. The employer also owes WCF and SDL. What is the net pay?
questions.explanation: Employee deductions total 150,000, so net pay is 900,000 - 150,000. Employer-only costs such as WCF and SDL are not taken from net pay.

questions.text: During review you find a teacher who left three months ago is still being paid, and the bank account details were changed last month. What is the best action?

options.text: Hold the payment, report to the finance manager and HR, and keep the records
Remove the name quietly from the list and tell nobody about the earlier payments
Call the former teacher and ask for a refund first
Wait for the year-end audit to raise it

questions.explanation: This may be fraud. Stop further payments, report promptly through the proper channel and preserve evidence for investigation.

questions.text: A staff member says her net pay is lower than expected and she does not recognise one deduction on the payslip. What should you do?

options.text: Tell her that payroll deductions are confidential and cannot be discussed with staff
Check the deduction against the signed authorisation and explain or correct it
Remove the deduction immediately without checking
Ask her to wait until next year's payroll

questions.explanation: Each deduction must be supported by law or the employee's written consent. Checking the record resolves the query and fixes any error.

questions.text: A new teacher starts work in the middle of the month. What do you need before adding the teacher to the payroll?

options.text: A verbal confirmation from the head teacher that the person has started work
Only the teacher's bank or mobile money number
Nothing until the probation period is over
An approved appointment letter plus identity, TIN and pension details

questions.explanation: New starters must be added using approved, documented terms and the details needed for tax and social security.

questions.text: Cash is tight this month. The head suggests delaying the remittance of PAYE and pension deductions to pay suppliers first. What is the best response?

options.text: Explain these amounts belong to the authorities and propose other options with the head
Agree to the delay and plan to pay both months together with next month's remittance
Agree, but record the deductions as already paid in the payroll system to avoid questions
Pay half and wait to see if the authorities ask

questions.explanation: Withheld statutory amounts are held for the authorities and must be paid on time. Delay creates penalties and legal risk, so alternatives (such as supplier terms) should be discussed.

questions.text: A teacher resigns and her last working day is the end of the month. Which payroll step is correct?

options.text: Remove her from payroll at once and pay nothing for the part of the month worked
Keep her on payroll for three more months
Pay final salary and entitlements per contract with statutory deductions, then stop her pay
Pay her final salary in full without any statutory deductions, because she is leaving the school

questions.explanation: Leavers are paid what is due under the contract, with the normal deductions and records, and then taken off the payroll.

description: Checks budget preparation, variance analysis, cash-flow forecasting, budget control and prioritisation skills.

competencies.name: Budget preparation
competencies.description: Prepares realistic income and expense budgets

competencies.name: Variance analysis
competencies.description: Calculates and explains budget variances

competencies.name: Cash-flow forecasting
competencies.description: Forecasts cash flow and manages timing gaps

competencies.name: Budget monitoring and control
competencies.description: Monitors spending and enforces approval controls

competencies.name: Prioritisation and planning
competencies.description: Prioritises requests when funds are limited

questions.text: What is a budget?

options.text: A report showing what the school earned and spent in the last financial year
A plan of expected income and spending for a future period
A list of all bank accounts of the school
A record of fees that parents have paid

questions.explanation: A budget is forward-looking: it sets expected income and planned spending so they can be controlled.

questions.text: Which information is needed to estimate next year's fee income? Select all that apply.

options.text: The approved fee per pupil
Expected number of pupils in each class
The cost of repairs done last year
The planned salary increase for teachers
Expected discounts, bursaries and unpaid fees

questions.explanation: Fee income depends on pupil numbers, fee levels and how much will actually be collected. Salaries and repairs are expenses.

questions.text: The electricity budget for the month is TZS 600,000 and the actual cost is TZS 540,000. What is the variance?

options.text: TZS 60,000 favourable
TZS 60,000 adverse
TZS 540,000 favourable
TZS 600,000 adverse

questions.explanation: Spending below budget is a favourable variance: 600,000 - 540,000 = 60,000.

questions.text: Budgeted fee income for the term was TZS 20,000,000. Actual fee income was TZS 17,000,000. What is the variance as a percentage of budget?

options.text: 15% favourable
17% adverse
15% adverse
3% adverse

questions.explanation: The shortfall is 3,000,000, which is 15% of 20,000,000. Income lower than budget is adverse.

questions.text: Why can a school with a budget surplus still run out of cash?

options.text: A surplus budget always creates the same amount of cash in the bank automatically
Cash problems only happen when the budget has a deficit
The bank takes the surplus at the end of each term
Fees may be collected late while expenses must be paid every month

questions.explanation: A budget shows totals, but a cash-flow forecast shows timing. Late collections and early payments can cause a cash shortage.

questions.text: Which items belong in a monthly cash-flow forecast? Select all that apply.

options.text: Depreciation of school vehicles
A bank loan instalment due in the month
The allowance for doubtful debts
Fees expected to be collected in the month
Salaries paid at month-end

questions.explanation: Cash-flow forecasts include actual cash movements. Depreciation and allowances are non-cash accounting entries.

questions.text: Which best describes zero-based budgeting?

options.text: Last year's budget is carried forward and increased by a fixed percentage each year
Planned income is set exactly equal to planned spending
Each budget line must be justified again every period, starting from zero
The budget is changed every month to match actual results

questions.explanation: In zero-based budgeting nothing is assumed from last year, so each cost must be justified and approved afresh.

questions.text: Halfway through the year, maintenance spending is 40% above budget because a storm damaged the roof. What is the best action?

options.text: Investigate, report the cause to management and ask for approved reallocation or extra funds
Ignore it, because it is a one-off event
Stop all maintenance until the new financial year starts, including urgent safety repairs
Reduce the recorded expense so that it matches the budget and the variance disappears from reports

questions.explanation: Variances should be explained and reported, with an approved decision on how to fund them. Records must never be changed to hide a variance.

questions.text: A department asks you to buy equipment costing TZS 2,000,000 that is not in the approved budget. What should you do?

options.text: Buy it now and move the cost to another budget line once the month is closed
Ask the requester to submit it for approval through the unbudgeted-expense procedure
Refuse every unbudgeted request under all circumstances, including urgent safety needs
Approve it directly, because the head of department has asked for it in writing

questions.explanation: Unbudgeted spending is possible, but only through the proper approval process and with a funding source identified.

questions.text: Your forecast shows a cash shortfall in two months because most fees arrive later. What is the best approach?

options.text: Wait until the shortfall actually happens, then ask the bank for an overdraft quickly
Use the exam fees already collected from parents to pay general expenses until fees arrive
Reduce staff salaries without telling them
Plan early: follow up arrears, negotiate supplier terms and delay non-essential spending

questions.explanation: A forecast lets you act before the shortfall. Money collected for a specific purpose, such as exams, should not be spent on other items.

questions.text: Budget requests total TZS 30 million, but only TZS 22 million is available. How should the requests be handled?

options.text: Rank them by priority and fund essential items first, such as safety and salaries
Cut every request by the same percentage so that each department is treated equally
Fund requests in the order in which they were received until the money is finished
Fund the requests from the most senior staff first, then the others if money remains

questions.explanation: Limited funds should go first to essential, high-priority needs agreed with stakeholders, not to equal cuts or first-come requests.

questions.text: The stationery budget is TZS 5,000,000. Spent so far: TZS 3,000,000. Approved orders not yet delivered: TZS 1,500,000. A new order of TZS 800,000 is requested. What is the correct conclusion?

options.text: TZS 2,000,000 is available, so the order can go ahead
TZS 3,500,000 is available, so the order can go ahead
Only TZS 500,000 is available, so the order needs extra approval
The order can go ahead, since only the money actually spent counts against the budget

questions.explanation: Available budget = 5,000,000 - 3,000,000 spent - 1,500,000 committed = 500,000. The 800,000 order exceeds it.

description: Checks school fee billing, receipting, arrears follow-up, mobile money and bank reconciliation, and fraud awareness.

competencies.name: Fee billing and receipting
competencies.description: Raises invoices and issues receipts in a controlled way

competencies.name: Arrears follow-up and payment plans
competencies.description: Follows up arrears, agrees plans and handles write-offs

competencies.name: Mobile money and bank reconciliation
competencies.description: Matches mobile money and bank payments to pupil accounts

competencies.name: Fraud awareness and controls
competencies.description: Recognises fraud risks and applies controls

competencies.name: Parent communication
competencies.description: Communicates respectfully with parents

questions.text: Why should fee receipts be numbered in sequence?

options.text: So parents can easily see how many other pupils have paid their fees in the same term
So every receipt is accounted for and missing or cancelled ones can be detected
So receipts look more professional to parents
So the bank can use them as payment proof

questions.explanation: Sequential numbering allows checks that all receipts issued are recorded and that none were removed or misused.

questions.text: What are "fee arrears"?

options.text: Fees that parents have paid in advance for terms that have not yet started
Fees refunded to parents after a transfer
Fees that the school has decided not to charge
Fees that were due but have not been paid by the due date

questions.explanation: Arrears are overdue amounts owed by parents or guardians.

questions.text: What is an ageing analysis of fee debtors?

options.text: A list of unpaid balances grouped by how long they have been overdue
A list of pupils with unpaid balances grouped by their age and class level
A report of payments grouped by payment method
A list of fees grouped by class and term

questions.explanation: Ageing shows which debts are older and riskier, so follow-up can be prioritised.

questions.text: Why should a bank deposit slip shown by a parent be confirmed on the bank statement before the account is marked as paid?

options.text: The bank statement is printed more clearly than slips and is easier to keep in files
The slip only shows the date and not the amount
The slip can be forged or altered, or the deposit may not have been completed
Parents are not allowed to make bank deposits for fees

questions.explanation: A slip is not proof that the money reached the school's account. Only the bank statement confirms receipt.

questions.text: Which details help match a mobile money payment to the right pupil? Select all that apply.

options.text: The pupil's admission or control number used as reference
The payer's phone number, amount and date
The pupil's home village
The number of subjects the pupil studies
The transaction ID given by the provider

questions.explanation: Unique references and payment details link a payment to an account. Personal details unrelated to the payment do not help matching.

questions.text: Which arrangement best reduces the risk of fraud in fee collection?

options.text: One trusted person receives, records and banks all the money to avoid confusion
Different people receive money, record it and reconcile the accounts
The head teacher personally counts all fees every day
Fees are kept in the office until the end of the week

questions.explanation: Separating duties means no single person can take money and hide it in the records.

questions.text: A family has left the country. After reasonable follow-up, TZS 1,200,000 of fees cannot be recovered. What is the correct treatment?

options.text: Delete the pupil's balance from the system quietly so that the debtors list looks clean
Move the amount to another pupil's account
Write it off with written approval from the authorised person and keep the record
Keep it on the current-term list forever

questions.explanation: Bad debts are written off only with documented approval, so the record stays visible and the process can be checked.

questions.text: A parent says she gave TZS 400,000 cash to the class teacher but has no receipt, and the school has not received it. What should you do?

options.text: Do not mark it paid; check with the teacher and remind parents of official channels
Mark it as paid, because the parent is a trusted and long-standing member of the school
Tell the parent that the loss is her own problem and that nothing can be done
Ask the teacher to give you cash from his own pocket to cover the amount

questions.explanation: Fees should be paid only to the cashier or official accounts with an official receipt. Check the facts before changing records.

questions.text: A mobile money payment of TZS 450,000 has the reference "Hassan". Two pupils named Hassan are in the school. What is the best action?

options.text: Allocate it to the Hassan who has the larger unpaid balance, since he owes the most money
Hold it as unallocated, contact the payer on the number shown and confirm which pupil
Split it equally between both pupils
Refund it to the sender straight away

questions.explanation: Never guess allocations. Confirm with the payer, and keep the money unallocated until it is identified.

questions.text: A parent says he paid TZS 800,000 to a number given by someone on WhatsApp who claimed to be the school accountant. What is the best action?

options.text: Credit the pupil's account in full, because the parent acted honestly and in good faith in the matter
Ask the parent to pay again and keep the receipt of the first
Ignore it, since the money did not come to the school
Check the number is not official, report to the head, and tell parents the official channels

questions.explanation: This is probably a scam. The school should confirm and report it, warn other parents and never credit money it did not receive.

questions.text: A parent who recently lost her job comes upset about an arrears notice, and she raises her voice in a busy office. What should you do?

options.text: Invite her to a private place, check her balance and explain the payment options
Ask her to leave the office now and to come back only when she has the money
Tell her loudly that rules apply to everyone
Remove her child's name from the class list until the full arrears have been paid

questions.explanation: Calm, private and respectful communication protects dignity and usually leads to a written payment plan under school policy.

questions.text: At month-end, fee receipts issued total TZS 12,500,000, but bank and mobile money credits for fees total TZS 12,200,000. What is the best action?

options.text: Reduce the receipts total by TZS 300,000 so that the two totals will agree again at month-end
Wait until the end of the year to check the difference
Match each receipt to a credit and investigate every unmatched item before adjusting
Add TZS 300,000 as a cash payment to balance it

questions.explanation: A difference means some receipts may not have been banked or some credits are unrecorded. Item-by-item matching finds the cause.

description: Checks purchasing procedures, supplier selection, goods receiving, stock control and asset management.

competencies.name: Purchasing procedures and approvals
competencies.description: Follows purchasing procedures, approvals and conflict-of-interest rules

competencies.name: Quotations, tenders and supplier selection
competencies.description: Obtains quotations and selects suppliers fairly

competencies.name: Receiving and inspecting goods
competencies.description: Inspects and records deliveries and matches documents

competencies.name: Stock control and stores records
competencies.description: Keeps stock records, controls issues and investigates differences

competencies.name: Asset management
competencies.description: Manages assets and their disposal

questions.text: Which document is sent to a supplier to formally order goods?

options.text: A goods received note from the store
A local purchase order (LPO)
A purchase requisition from the department
A stock card kept in the store

questions.explanation: The LPO is the approved order sent to the supplier. A requisition is only an internal request.

questions.text: Why does a school obtain several quotations before buying expensive items?

options.text: To make sure that the offer with the lowest price is always accepted by the school
To delay the purchase until the budget is approved
To give every supplier in the area some business
To compare price and quality and obtain value for money

questions.explanation: Competitive quotations help a school choose the best offer and reduce favouritism.

questions.text: Which body regulates public procurement in Tanzania?

options.text: Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA)
Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
National Examinations Council (NECTA)
Tanzania Communications Regulatory Authority (TCRA)

questions.explanation: PPRA is the regulator of public procurement, which public schools and other public bodies must follow.

questions.text: Which documents should be compared before a supplier is paid (the three-way match)?

options.text: Requisition, quotation and bank statement
Delivery note, stock card and the monthly payroll summary
Purchase order, goods received note and supplier invoice
Invoice, tender notice and the supplier's business licence

questions.explanation: Payment should be made only if the goods ordered, the goods actually received and the amount invoiced agree.

questions.text: Which details should a stock card (bin card) show? Select all that apply.

options.text: The supplier's bank account number
The running balance after each movement
Quantities received and issued, with dates and references
Item description and unit of measure
The depreciation rate of the item

questions.explanation: A stock card tracks the movement and balance of one item. Payment and depreciation details belong in other records.

questions.text: Which issuing method should the school kitchen use for food items that can expire?

options.text: Last in, first out
First expiry, first out (FEFO)
Issue whichever is easiest to reach
Issue the newest stock first

questions.explanation: FEFO issues the items that will expire soonest first, reducing waste.

questions.text: What is the correct way to dispose of an old school computer that no longer works?

options.text: Give it to any staff member who asks for it and tell the storekeeper afterwards
Let the storekeeper sell it to whoever offers the best cash price today, keeping the money
Obtain written approval, dispose of it properly and update the asset register
Throw it away and delete it from the asset register without any approval

questions.explanation: Disposals need authorisation and records, so assets cannot be taken privately and the register stays accurate.

questions.text: The head asks you to buy three laptops for TZS 4,500,000 from his relative without quotations. What is the best response?

options.text: Insist on quotations, declare the conflict of interest and follow approval rules
Buy them as asked, since the head has the final authority over all school spending
Split the order into three smaller orders so that each stays below the approval limit
Ask the relative to bring two other quotations from friends so the file looks complete

questions.explanation: Procurement must be fair and transparent. Conflicts of interest must be declared, and splitting orders or fake quotations breaks the rules.

questions.text: A delivery note shows 50 bags of rice, but three bags are torn when delivered. What should you do?

options.text: Sign for all 50 bags to avoid delays and raise the problem with the supplier later
Count and inspect, record the accepted bags, note the damage and inform the supplier
Refuse the whole delivery without writing anything
Accept 50 bags and repair the torn ones yourself

questions.explanation: Goods are accepted only after checking quantity and condition. Damage must be recorded on the delivery documents for a replacement or credit.

questions.text: A stock count shows 20 fewer exercise books than the stock card. What is the best action?

options.text: Adjust the stock card quietly so that it matches the physical count and the file is clean
Ask the storekeeper to replace the books
Ignore it, since it is a small difference and the books will probably be found later
Recount, check unrecorded issues or returns and report the variance before adjusting

questions.explanation: Differences should be investigated first. Any adjustment needs approval and a documented reason.

questions.text: Quotation A is TZS 1,200,000 but does not meet the specification. Quotation B is TZS 1,300,000 and meets it. What is the best decision?

options.text: Choose B, because A is not compliant with the specification
Choose A, because the lowest price always wins
Choose B only if the supplier gives a personal gift
Ask both suppliers to reduce prices by negotiating in secret

questions.explanation: Offers are first checked against the specification. The best choice is the lowest-priced offer that meets the requirements.

questions.text: The storekeeper is on leave and a teacher takes items from the store without a requisition. What is the correct approach?

options.text: Allow it, because the teacher is a trusted colleague
Allow it if the teacher promises to inform the storekeeper about the items later
Issue items only against an approved requisition and record every issue
Let the cleaners hold the store keys for the day

questions.explanation: Stores issues must be authorised and recorded to avoid losses and to keep stock records accurate.
